The method constructs the optimal embedding space and restores the dynamic characteristics of performance degradation of radar, by which the maximum predictable number of steps based on the largest Lyapunov exponent can be calculated to determine whether the performance observation parameters can be predicted. Furthermore, scientific basis of determining a valid time advance can be provided. Finally, the experimental analysis of radar signal-to-noise ratio parameter observation sequences was carried out, indicating that the proposed method is effective for radar equipment.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation of In-use HFC Relative Degradation Degree Based on Mixed Weight Adjustment Method and Substitution Synthesis Method
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: In order to determine the degradation degree of in-use Water glycol fire-resistant hydraulic fluids (HFC) to grasp the oil change and replenishment timing, the mixed weight adjustment method and substitution synthesis method were applied to the comprehensive evaluation of HFC degradation degree. Based on the four design functions: anti-combustion, lubrication, anti-corrosion, and power transmission, the monitoring indicators were reduced, and an HFC monitoring indicators system including four indicators: moisture content, viscosity, pH, and contamination level was constructed. The trigonometric function, incremental exponential function and decreasing exponential function were respectively applied to the relative degradation degree assessment of moisture content and viscosity, contamination level, and PH. The subjective and objective weights of indicators were calculated by analytic hierarchy process and entropy method, and then combined and adjusted by the mixed weight adjustment method. The comprehensive relative degradation degree was synthesized by substitution synthesis method. The analysis example shows that the mixed weight adjustment method can achieve the "promoting good and punishing poor" function and the substitution synthesis method can meet the "one-vote veto" mechanism in oil monitoring. A more accurate comprehensive evaluation of HFC relative degradation degree could be made by mixed weight adjustment method and substitution synthesis method.

Author Keywords: water glycol fire-resistant hydraulic fluids, relative degradation degree, comprehensive evaluation, analytic hierarchy process, entropy method, mixed weight adjustment method, substitution synthesis method

articleTitle: The Design of the Hand Structure of a Kind of Exoskeleton Type Maintenance Power-Assisted Gloves
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: In view of the current situation in which a large number of maintenance tasks impose a heavy burden on the hands, this project proposes the development of a kind of maintenance power-assisted gloves that will provide auxiliary grip strength through the exoskeleton structure. In this paper, the design of the hand exoskeleton structure of the gloves is introduced in detail, and the current maintenance field needs are taken as the design goal. The exoskeleton structure was designed and improved from the perspective of bionics, and the movement of the exoskeleton structure was analyzed through theoretical study and analysis as well as simulation. Finally, experiments were performed to verify the power-assisted performance of the exoskeleton structure.

Author Keywords: maintenance assistance, exoskeleton, structural design, bionics

articleTitle: Current-Based Gear Fault Detection for Locomotive Gearboxes
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Our objective is to analyze the traction motor stator current in the diagnosis of the gearbox fault of the locomotive. The gear localized defects cause torque oscillations which modulate the frequency components in the stator current signal and generate the sidebands in the stator current power spectrum. However, the sideband components are weak and covered by noise. Dual-tree complex wavelet transform is used to extract fault features hidden in the sidebands. We use wavelet energy entropy to make a preliminary diagnosis of the signal, and then apply a dual-tree complex wavelet transform in the current signal to further determine the type of failure. In order to illustrate the validity of the proposed diagnosis method, simulation signal analysis was carried out and then verified in the laboratory. Finally, gear diagnosis experiments on the freight locomotive show that the proposed method can effectively diagnose gear failures.

Author Keywords: gearbox, motor stator current analysis, dual tree complex wavelet transform, gear fault diagnosis

articleTitle: Degradation Model of Photovoltaic Modules Under Multi-Environment Factors Coupling Based on FEM and Failure Physical Model
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Degradation of photovoltaic (PV) module is effected by environment factors such as ambient temperature, ambient humidity, solar irradiation, wind speed and complicated coupling effects. Therefore, the performance degradation is difficult to be accurately assessed, especially for the output power of PV modules. Based on Finite Element Method (FEM) and failure physical model, a degradation model of output power is proposed, where environment factors and coupling effects are considered. First, based on monitoring environment data, the physical field of the PV module is simulated using FEM. Then, module temperature and module humidity are obtained based on the results of physical field simulation. Putting module temperature and module humidity into the failure physical model, the performance degradation rate is obtained. Finally, a degradation model of output power is obtained by combining the output power and degradation rate. The effect of diffusion coefficient on output power degradation is analyzed by varying the diffusion coefficient. Results show that effects of ambient temperature on module temperature and diffusion process cannot be ignored, and the effect of diffusion coefficient on output power degradation is nonlinear.

Author Keywords: photovoltaic module, degradation model of output power, Finite Element Method, failure physical model

articleTitle: A Particle Filtering Based Approach for Transformer Winding Degradation Prognostics
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: When the transformer works for a long time, its winding is gradually deteriorated with time, and the fault phenomena such as winding short circuit or circuit break lead to serious power supply accidents. Under high temperature conditions, this paper analyzes the degradation process of the winding, and determines that the resonant frequency can be used as testing index of its degradation process. Therefore, the resonant frequency is used to monitor the performance degradation state of the transformer winding and realize the advance prediction, which can effectively avoid accidents. Accurate prediction of system reliability is of plenty of importance to engineering systems for accomplishing the designate function and system safety management. As the concerned system is getting complicated and more sufficient health monitoring measurement is available, the traditional reliability prediction schemes resorting to only one kind of prediction approaches, model-based or data-driven, begin to show their limitations. This paper proposes a PF prognostic method by combining traditional model approaches. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by thermal degradation experiments. This method improves the reliability of power system and is conducive to the rapid development of smart grid.

Author Keywords: degeneration, insulation failure, PF, resonant frequency, premature prognostic

articleTitle: An Age-State-Dependent Degradation Model
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Degradation modeling plays a key role in accelerated degradation test data analysis and condition-based maintenance. The degradation rate of a degradation process usually depends on both unit's age and its state. Several agestate-dependent degradation models have been proposed in the literature. A main drawback of these models is their intractability. In this paper, we propose an analytically tractable age-state-dependent degradation model. The proposed model is defined in terms of degradation rate, whose mean function is represented by a bivariate power-law model. The degradation increment is modeled by a non-homogeneous gamma process, whose mean function depends on both age and degradation level and has a closed-form expression. The model includes age-and state-dependent models as its special cases. An approach is proposed to make selection among the general case and special cases based on the Akaike information criterion. A real-world example is used to illustrate the flexibility and usefulness of the proposed model and approach.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Piezoresistive Graphene/HBN Heterostructure Pressure Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: High precision pressure sensor is a common sensing device for condition monitoring and fault prediction. 2-D materials such as graphene and boron nitride have excellent mechanical property, which provide an effective technical approach for developing high precision pressure sensors. However, the design of current suspended piezoresistive graphene/h-BN heterostructure pressure sensor is mainly based on experience and lacks sensitivity model guidance when designing the structure size. On the basis of modeling and simulation results of membrane deformation, the relationship among membrane resistance, size and ambient pressure is derived. The sensitivity model of circular membrane is established, based on which the structure size of the sensor is designed. The graphene/h-BN heterostructure is obtained via wet transfer technology with a series of membrane diameters fabricated. The test results show that the proposed sensitivity model and manufacturing process are effective and reasonable.

articleTitle: Efficiency Optimization of MIMO Magnetic Induction Communication Systems Based on Voltage Modulation
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: In the magnetic induction (MI) communication system, the traditional circular coil is sensitive to the angle change, so it is impossible to transmit signal to the receiving antenna at certain deflection angles. This paper analyzes the effect of the excitation voltage of each transmitting antenna element in the coil array on the coupling efficiency of the system by changing the phase and amplitude. Using the genetic algorithm, the optimal input voltage of the transmitting antenna for a certain position/deflection angle of antenna which is aimed to increase the coupling efficiency is obtained. Without increasing the transmit power, the received power and the signal-to-noise ratio are increased, so the system communication quality is improved. In this paper, a simple three-transmission coil array antenna is taken as an example. By adjusting the amplitude and phase of the three coil excitation voltages respectively, the enhancement of the system's coupling efficiency with the receiving antenna in a certain position or deflection angle has been achieved as a result. And the research has enhanced the magnetic induction communication systems' angular adaptability to the receiving antenna.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Method Based on the Condition Indicators of Compressive Sampling for the Gearbox in Helicopter
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: In the field of condition monitoring and fault diagnosis of rotating machinery, it is always necessary to monitor the component uninterruptedly for a long period of time. This process will generate masses of original data which would burden the storage and transmission. In data analysis, we can decode the compressed data we saved to recover the original vibration data and implement fault detection and diagnosis etc. with relevant available methods. The majority of the original data would be dropped, which should be an enormous waste of resources. Since the signal can be compressed, we should consider whether we can obtain compressive sampling data directly and omit much data containing useless information at the same time. This idea is the rudiment of compressed sampling. The general method for gearbox fault detection is achieved by using vibration signals which sampled in the frame of Shannon sampling theory. For this issue, a fault detection method based on compressed sampling theory is proposed in this paper. A condition indicator is extracted based on the measurements of the reconstruction deviation, and these reconstruction signal sets are all based on the normal redundant dictionary. The availability and effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through the simulation data sets with different faults seeded.

articleTitle: A Study of Helicopter Structural Damage Monitoring Technology Based-on Synthetic Time-Reversal Imaging Method
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The structural health monitoring technology and its system based on piezoelectric transducers and Lamb waves were studied for the urgent demand of damage detection for aircraft composite structures. This article proposed an identification algorithm of structural damage based on synthetic time-reversal imaging method, designed the active structural health monitoring system, and carried out experiment on structures of helicopter tail boom. The analysis results have shown that the monitoring system could be reliable, stable and sensitive to the damages within the millimeter scale. Additionally, the influence of excitation parameters on the diagnostic accuracy of damage localization is also discussed.

Author Keywords: structural health monitoring, piezoelectric transducer network, active Lamb waves, synthetic time-reversal imaging, damage detection

articleTitle: Effects of Welded Pores on Fatigue Life of Titanium Alloy Electron-Beam Welded Joints
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The welded pore is one of common defects in titanium alloy electron-beam welded (EBW) joints and significantly influences its fatigue life. In this paper, effect of the welded pore on fatigue life of titanium alloy EBW joints were studied through an experimental investigation. Fatigue tests and fracture observation were conducted for EBW joints. Results showed that the welded pore is the most possible crack initiation. Through quantitative analysis on pore size and depth, a model was established to characterize the effect of initiation pore on fatigue life based on S-N model. Moreover, the effect of pore scatter on fatigue life scatter was investigated based on Monte-Carlo simulations, and the results indicated that scatter of pore size and depth is the key factor contributing to the wide scatter of fatigue life of welded joints.

articleTitle: Intelligent Maintenance Design of Nuclear Power System Based on PHM
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Nuclear power plant is a complex and huge system. There are interrelated, coupling and nonlinear relations between the systems. The rapid location, detection and maintenance of nuclear power plant failures is an important way to improve the safety and reliability of the system. Precise and fast fault detection device has become an important part of nuclear power plants. In this paper, a fault diagnosis strategy based on the fault propagation model based on the directed graph analysis for nuclear power plant is proposed. The fault diagnosis model is suitable for the single fault and multi fault situation of the system. According to the nuclear power system operation process, operation conditions, complex dynamic characteristics, and the qualitative logic relation between variables to maintain the basic characteristics of stable, the proposed diagnosis model for fault diagnosis, diagnostic reasoning method have incomparable advantage compared with other graph models. Besides, for the modules or units involved in the nuclear power system, a knowledge supplement based on probability and statistics is applied to achieve blind spot diagnosis and location.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling of Two-Component System with Degradation Interaction Based on Copulas
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The stochastic dependency exists in many complex systems, which cannot be ignored in reliability modeling. The stochastic dependency is analyzed from the degradation perspective in this paper. For a two-component system, a degradation interaction model is built to describe the dependency between the degradations of two components based on nonlinear Wiener process and Copula function. Then, the reliability functions of components and system are derived, and the parameter estimation approach of the developed models is given. Finally, a numerical example about fatigue crack development is presented to validate and illustrate the performance of the developed models.

articleTitle: Gear Fault Diagnosis Based on EEMD-CWD with K-CC Criteria
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: To improve the accuracy of the joint time-frequency analysis method for mechanical fault diagnosis, a gear fault diagnosis method, which combined with ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and Choi-Williams distribution (CWD), is proposed in this paper. First, the collected faulty gear vibration signal is decomposed into a series of intrinsic modal components (IMFs) by EEMD, and IMFs are ranked in descending order of frequency. Then, the false components are removed and IMFs, which are "sensitive" to gear fault features, are selected based on the criteria of Kurtosis (K) and Cross-Correlation (CC). Finally, the selected IMFs are expressed in CWD Spectrogram, and the frequency and periodical impact features in time-frequency domain are combined to identify the gear fault characteristics. The applicability and effectiveness of this proposed method for gearbox gear fault diagnosis are verified by simulation and experimental analysis.

articleTitle: Ball Screw Stability Degradation Stages Evaluation Based on Deep Residual Neural Network and Multi-sensor Fusion
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to evaluate the degradation stages of stability of the screw with data fusion technology and deep residual neural network. Firstly, the data provided by multi-sensors are fused, and then the time domain images of the signals are input into the deep residual neural network for training and testing. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using data sets collected from the degradation test bench of ball screw. The data sets contain massive samples involving 3 degradation stages under 9 working conditions obtained by 3 accelerometers. From the results and comparison, it can be found that the deep residual neural network can automatically extract the features from the original data layer by layer and achieve a better evaluation rate when it is used to evaluate the performance stage of the screw, and the multi-sensor data fusion vibration data can better reflect the degradation stages of the screw's performance. It is showed that this method enhances the intelligence of the evaluation compared with the traditional method.

Author Keywords: Deep residuals neural network, Multi-sensor data fusion, Performance evaluation, Degradation recognition

articleTitle: Analyzing Accelerated Degradation Data via an Inverse Gaussian Degradation Model with Random Parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: A degradation model with random parameters can improve the accuracy of reliability assessment compared with that with fixed parameters. However, it is difficult to apply the degradation model with random parameters to straightforwardly analyze accelerated degradation data. To overcome this problem, a method applying the random parameter Inverse Gaussian degradation model to analyze accelerated degradation data was studied in this paper. Acceleration factor constant principle was used to deduce the relationships that the parameters of Inverse Gaussian degradation model should satisfy under different stresses. Then, the expression of acceleration factor for an inverse Gaussian degradation model was obtained. The degradation data under accelerated stress levels was transformed to the equivalent degradation data under the normal stress level based on acceleration factors. The conjugate prior distributions of random parameters were applied and Expectation Maximization algorithm was designed to estimate hyper parameters. Simulation tests validated the feasibility and effectiveness of proposed method, and a case study demonstrated the proposed method has a good engineering application value.

Author Keywords: Reliability, accelerated degradation test, random parameter, Inverse Gaussian, acceleration factor

articleTitle: An Iterative Parameters Estimator for Damped Exponential Signal in Noise
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The paper proposed a hybrid-iteration algorithm to estimate the parameters (frequency and damping factor) of damped exponential signal. With regard to core idea of this method, the new algorithm utilizes the phase difference based on asymmetric window as the first implementation and interpolation Discrete Fourier Transform (IpDFT) as the second one. The estimator introduces the asymmetric phase difference method to the decaying case and avoids the error generated from wrong location of spectral line. The root mean squares error (RMSE) was investigated in the case of white Gauss noise to evaluate the capability of robustness against adaptive noise. Extensive numerical simulations show that the RMSEs of the proposed algorithm closely attach to Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). In addition, simulation results also indicate that the new method has excellent performance against random noise compared with other interpolation DFT algorithms.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Detection in Varying Operational Conditions Based on Empirical Mode Decomposition and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Roller bearings play a significant role in kinds of machine. In most cases, it won't work in steadily operational conditions. The paper proposed a method which combines empirical mode decomposition and auto-regressive model to extract features of faults in various operational conditions and uses random forests to set an effective pattern recognition model. In addition, the paper compares the result of random forests with that of some other classification method. The bearing vibration data comes from Case Western Reserve University Bearing Data Center. The result indicates that the method is effective and can be used in actual situations.

articleTitle: A Warranty Policy for Repairable Products with Bathtub-Shape Failure Rate
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: This study proposes a warranty policy for repairable products with bathtub-shape failure rate. Based on bathtub-shape curve, the warranty period is divided into two stages. In the first stage, the failure rate is non-increasing. In the second stage, the failure rate is strictly increasing, and imperfect preventive maintenance actions are carried out periodically. All the failures occurring over the warranty period are restored by minimal repair. Two-fold Weibull competing risk model is used to describe the bathtub-shape curve. The warranty cost, which is fully paid by the manufacturer, is analyzed. A numerical optimization method is presented to achieve the optimal preventive maintenance strategy so as to minimize the warranty cost. A numerical example with actual failure data is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed policy. The results show that the manufacturer can benefit from the proposed policy, and more cost will be saved if the minimal repair cost is higher.

Author Keywords: bathtub-shape failure rate, preventive maintenance, warranty policy, two-fold Weibull competing risk model

articleTitle: The Bio-Objective Long Term Maintenance Scheduling for Wind Turbines Considering Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Effective maintenance scheduling for wind turbines (WTs) has become an essential issue nowadays due to the high maintenance cost of wind energy industry. Comparing with thermal generators, the maintenance of WTs is significantly affected by weather conditions. This paper focuses on finding the optimal long term maintenance schedules for wind farms considering weather conditions. A statistical model to predict weather conditions (e.g., wind speed and the probability of rainfall) is developed. A bio-objective Genetic Algorithm is developed to identify maintenance schedules that incur low labor cost and production loss. A practical study is also presented to validate the proposed methods.

Author Keywords: long term maintenance scheduling, optimization, Genetic Algorithms, wind energy, weather data prediction

articleTitle: Condition Based Maintenance of the Yaw Motor in a Wind Turbine Using an Indirect Indicator: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Currently, the tremendous failure cost restricts the rapid development of wind energy industry. Condition based maintenance is one of the most effective strategies to reduce the maintenance cost of wind turbines. However, this paper aims to develop a maintenance optimization model based on the prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) of yaw motor that is an important component of a wind turbine. A practical case is considered rather than theoretical models that most of the existing studies dealt with. The prediction accuracy of RUL is greatly improved with an indirect indicator. Both the maintenance optimization models of preventive activities and opportunistic activities are proposed. The developed methods are expected to bring valuable benefits to the wind energy industry and provide reference for the maintenance of yaw motors in a wind turbine.

Author Keywords: condition based maintenance, yaw motors, remaining useful life, opportunistic maintenance

articleTitle: GKFP: A New Fuzzy Clustering Method Applied to Bearings Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: This paper proposes a new clustering method called Gustafson-Kessel with Focal Point (GKFP). The proposal aims at benefiting from the advantage of using Gustafson-Kessel clustering technique leveraged by the use of a Focal Point which enables obtaining partitions with different levels of granularity. Thus the method identifies clusters with uncorrelated or strongly correlated data while it allows the user to explore different regions of the feature space with different levels of detail. Due to the possibility of dealing with correlated data, a regularization procedure might be necessary. Therefore, the paper also briefly describes a Bayesian regularization which can be associated with GKFP. Experiments from bearing fault diagnosis show that GKFP outperforms three other clustering techniques, i.e., the popular fuzzy c-means (FCM), Gustafson-Kessel (GK), and the state of the art FCMFP, for two different bearing data sets.

Author Keywords: clustering, fuzzy covariance matrix, GKFP, Bayes Inference

articleTitle: Research on Classification Methods of LOS for Urban Rail Transit Stations Passages
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: In order to classify the level of service (LOS) for urban rail transit station passages, the paper proposes a passengers' perception correction method based on Gaussian mixture model. Based on pedestrian average occupancy space as a standard of classification, a Gaussian mixture model is established based on the flow, density, and speed of the passenger flow, and a preliminary classification is performed. Then, based on the passenger perception design questionnaire, the classification threshold of the mathematical model is corrected. We use the actual passenger flow data of Guangzhou Metro to verify the model and compare it with the TCQSM (II). It verifies the practicability of the model.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Performance Prognostics and Health Management Platform for Weapon Equipment
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The application of prognostics and health management (PHM) technology for complex weapon equipment has been a hot research topic in recent years. In order to solve the problems of low data utilization, expensive prognostics and health management methods, and high real-time requirements in engineering, it is necessary to build a comprehensive platform to implement the PHM functions. This paper introduces a high-performance prognostics and health management platform which can be effectively used to assess and predict the performance of weapon equipment. The platform is based on DSP + FPGA collaborative computing acceleration architecture, and can accelerate PHM data processing tasks by using the co-processing card containing DSPs and FPGAs. The platform has the capabilities to acquire multi-channel high-speed data, and convert the data into health-related information and maintenance decision. The health information and maintenance decision can then be integrated into the software for interface displaying. An application example is used to validate that the platform can be applied to prognostic applications of weapon equipment and is high-performance.

Author Keywords: weapon equipment, prognostics and health management platform, collaborative computing, DSP, FPGA

articleTitle: Study of Structural Reliability Evaluation Method Based on Deep BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The back propagation (BP) neural network is commonly used to detect the fault of some equipment in the actual project. When the fault data is sufficient, BP neural network has achieved good results. But for practical engineering, it commonly meets with the rare failure event. The proposed detection model based on deep BP neural network in this paper is not only applicable to the case of sufficient fault data, but also applies to the rare fault data. In this structure reliability analysis, samples generated by Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) are usually safe samples and the failure samples are very rare. The case is similar to the rare event in engineering. In this paper, a detection model based on deep BP neural network will be proposed to deal with the rare failure samples generated by MCS and calculate the failure probability. Finally, the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method are demonstrated by a numerical example and an engineering application.

Author Keywords: deep BP neural network, structure reliability, Monte Carlo Simulation, failure probability

articleTitle: A Novel Weak Bearing Fault Detection Method Based on Vibrational Resonance
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Weak-fault detection is difficult due to the disturbance of strong background noise and low signal-to-noise ratio. In this paper, we investigate the application of vibrational resonance to weak-fault detection. Different from the denoising methods, vibrational resonance can enhance the weak-fault signal with the cooperation of high-frequency interferences. Compared with another noise-utilization method, stochastic resonance, vibrational resonance is more controllable. Due to the adiabatic approximation condition, the original bistable system based on vibrational resonance is effective for those signals whose frequencies are much less than 1 Hz. In order to overcome the limitation, a frequency-shifted and rescaling-transform method is introduced. The fruit fly optimization algorithm is introduced to optimize the parameter in the bistable system. The proposed vibrational resonance based weak-fault detection method is validated by simulation signal and experimental bearing fault dataset. The results show the better performance in terms of resonated amplitude and signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Algorithm Implementation of Data Acquisition System of Fiber Bragg Grating Demodulator Based on Compressive Sampling
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: According to the demodulation of high frequency vibration signal in the FBG (Fiber Bragg Grating) demodulator, the sampling frequency of the demodulator is high. And the high frequency sampling circuit designed in the practical application has the problem of high cost and unstable system. Therefore, the compressive sampling method is introduced into the FBG demodulator to replace the traditional Nyquist sampling for the compressive sampling of the reflection spectrum signal of FBG. This method reduces the sampling frequency requirement of data acquisition system by compressing data. In this paper, simulation experiments are used to verify the feasibility of compressive sampling. Through simulation experiments, the signal can still be reconstructed by algorithm when the data compressive ratio is 3.6:1. The MSE (mean-square error) of the reconstructed signal and the original signal is 0.0161, and the RE (relative error) near the peak value of the reconstructed signal is less than 0.009. Compared to directly reducing the sampling frequency, the reconstruction error of compressive sampling is much smaller than that of low-frequency sampling. In addition, through simulation experiments, it was found that compressive sampling can reconstruct signals under certain noise.

articleTitle: The Influence of Force and Magnetic Field on the Self-Sensing Characteristics of Magneto-Rheological Elastomer Bearing
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: A new self-sensing bearing based on magneto-rheological elastomers (MREs) was proposed in this paper. For the application in vibration isolation system, the effects of force field and magnetic field on the self-sensing characteristics were simultaneously investigated. Based on the modified MRE, the small-scaled bearing experimental system was built. The results confirmed that the bearing has excellent transient response ability when subjected to impact load and magnetic field (applied by a controlled current). The self-sensing characteristic presents a monotonous decline trend with well linearity. This finding is significant because it suggests that the bearings based on the modified MREs are potentially capable of being used for vibration absorbers and sensor simultaneously. It's a valuable way to simplify the system structure and improve the response performance of vibration isolation.

Author Keywords: Magneto-rheological elastomer bearing, Multi walled carbon nanotubes, Piezoresistive, Multi-field coupling, Self-sensing characteristics

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Multi-scale Entropy for Centrifugal Pump
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: To solve the problem of difficulty in extracting fault features from the vibration signal of centrifugal pump, this paper proposes an integrated method based on multi-scale entropy (MSE) and local characteristic-scale decomposition (LCD) for centrifugal pump fault diagnosis. Firstly, LCD is applied to decompose the signal into a series of components. Secondly, MSE is extracted as the signal feature. Thirdly, probabilistic neural network (PNN) is employed for fault recognition. Finally, a case is studied based on the experimental data of a centrifugal pump, and the present method achieves the accuracy of 98.00%. Compared with other fault diagnostic methods, the proposed approach exhibits the best performance. The results validate the effectiveness and superiority of the present method.

articleTitle: The Influence Study of Time-Varying Stiffness on the Vibration Impact of Planetary Gear Set System
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Planetary gear sets are widely used in the transmission system. Multiple time-varying stiffness from sun-planet and planet-ring meshing areas leads to multiple meshing impacts, but researches on the relationship between the multiple stiffness and the impacts are still superficial. To have a further study, the time-varying stiffness and a 18 degree of freedom dynamic model of a planetary gear set were built respectively in this paper. First the sun-planet pair meshing stiffness was compared when different level of crack happened in a sun and planet gear respectively. The results show that meshing stiffness variation decreases more when the cracked level increases. While for a certain crack level, the decrease variation increases when cracked on sun gear while the variation decreases when cracked on planet gear with the system running. Then the connection between meshing stiffness mutation and system impacts were studied when the gears were perfect. The results show that there are 4N times of impacts in a complete meshing period for a planetary gear set with N planets, and the impact amplitude generated from planet-ring meshing pair stiffness mutation is higher than that of the sun-planet meshing pair. Then the impacts starting moment and amplitude were analyzed to study the impacts influence caused by the sun gear fault. It is found that the impact initial point appears in the first single-tooth meshing duration of the fault sun-planet gear meshing pair when a small crack happens on the sun gear, which is induced by the suddenly increased stiffness of the planet-ring meshing pair. Besides, the fault impact amplitude increases with the fault level.

Author Keywords: Planetary gear set, time-varying meshing stiffness, vibration impact

articleTitle: Research on Gearbox On-line Diagnosis Based on Order Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The gearbox is the core component of the automobile transmission system. Analyzing and ensuring its assembly quality is an important part of the automobile production process. Order analysis method is an effective method to study the vibration of rotating machinery, and its analysis process is not affected by the change of rotating speed of the object. Aiming at the fault diagnosis of automobile gearbox, the use of order analysis method and its realization as well as the principle of equal-angle sampling was introduced. The order analysis of the fault gearbox was performed in the analyzing system. The result proves that the order analysis is feasible and effective for gearbox diagnosis.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Degradation Assessment for Urban Rail Traction Power Supply Equipment Considering Different Operation State
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the relative important degree of indexes will change, when urban rail power supply equipment is in different running state, this paper proposes a comprehensive degradation assessment model. The model uses the discrete degree of indexes' historical data to describe the relative importance of each indexes, and calculates the initial weights of each indexes by mean variance method (MVM). When the equipment is in normal operation state, the initial weight is corrected by the current detection data of the index, and the comprehensive degradation degree of the equipment is obtained. According to the principle of "more value punishment", when the equipment is in failure state, the weight of the index can be reassigned by the variable weight formula to realize the comprehensive assessment of the degradation degree of the equipment. Finally, the effectiveness of the comprehensive assessment method is verified by an example.

Author Keywords: urban rail, traction power supply equipment, comprehensive degradation assessment, different operation state

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis for Bolted Beam with Nonlinear Behaviors of Joint Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: A method combining the Newton-Raphson iteration process with the multi-harmonic balance method (MHBM) is proposed to analyze the steady-state dynamic response of the bolted beam system. The modified Iwan model is used to describe the nonlinear behaviors of the joint interfaces, and applied to construct the dynamical governing equations of a vibration system. The proposed MHBM is used to calculate the frequency response function (FRF) of a lap-type bolted beam with the nonlinear behaviors of joint interface. The simulating results are verified by a comparison with numerical integration solution, and the effects of nonlinear joint stiffness parameter are also investigated. The results show that the solutions obtained by the proposed harmonic balance method agree well with the direct numerical integration solution. The FRF can exhibit the effect of nonlinear softening stiffness and nonlinear damping of joint interface.

Author Keywords: joint interfaces, steady-state response, multi harmonic balance method, frequency response function

articleTitle: A Fuzzy Bayesian Based Zero-Failure Accelerated Life Demonstration Test Design Method
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The zero-failure accelerated degradation demonstration (ADD) test method is employed to verify the product reliability. Generally, the parameter of the acceleration model is assumed to be known in advance. However, the epistemic uncertainty due to the discrepancy of lifetime distribution between the earlier test unit and current products should be taken into consideration. Besides, the epistemic uncertainty due to small sample also leads to an inaccurate estimation. Therefore, it is worth to consider these two epistemic uncertainties above and the random uncertainties caused by random effects in time dimension and unit-to-unit variations. In this paper, a fuzzy Bayesian based zero-failure accelerated degradation demonstration (ADD) test method is proposed. This method takes the three uncertainties into account and is optimized based on the target of minimizing the test cost with a minimum sample size. An electrical power panel zero-failure ADD test is presented to illustrate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Interconnected Structures Failure of Electronic Packaging Under Vibration Load
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: In order to effectively acquire the comparable vibration degradation test data of interconnection structures in electronic packaging, problems which may exist in the reliability test of electronic packaging are analyzed in depth, using the existing environmental testing standards and combining with the accumulated experience in practical electronic reliability experiments. A complete set of degradation test methods for vibration failure of interconnected structures was proposed. This method can give a complete solution for the failure test of the interconnection structure in electronic packaging. Analysis of experimental data shows that the test data can well characterize the degradation process of the interconnected structures, and the outside interconnection structures in electronic packaging are easier to fail than the inside interconnection structures. The experimental method can effectively guide the implementation of the degradation test in the field of electronic interconnected structures in electronic packaging.

Author Keywords: experimental research, random vibration, failure, interconnected structure, package

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Fuel Consumption of DENA Vehicle Based on Side Window Condition
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Scientist recent researches indicate that humans are responsible for environmental effects through the mass usage of fossil fuels. Beyond engine efficiency and vehicle-related parameters-that should be checked and maintained periodically for efficient fuel consumption-there are some other effective parameters related to driving conditions. So, it is obvious that the value of measured consumption under real-world condition differs from that provided by a car manufacturer. Among all these parameters it is decided to choose and study the side window condition. Therefore, some experimental tests on DENA vehicle have been executed in order to mathematically model fuel consumption as a function of chosen parameters. This model has been finally validated by some data that has not been used in modeling procedure.

Author Keywords: Fuel consumption, modelling, greenhouse gases, environmental effects

articleTitle: Weighted Probabilistic Neural Network Based on the Sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Due to low training complexity, high stability, quick convergence and simple construction, the probabilistic neural network (PNN) has got extensive application in many fields. Because of the lack of additional weighting factors inside PNN model structure, the PNN using the Sensitivity Analysis (SA) has been improved in this paper. The weight coefficients and compensating factors are introduced into the network and put between pattern layer and summation layer to create the weighted probabilistic neural network (WPNN). The weights are derived using the sensitivity analysis procedure when the radial kernels are used as the output of the pattern layer. At the same time, compensating factors compensate the impact of the SA among the patterns. The performance of the WPNN is examined in contradistinctive experiments. Meanwhile, WPNN is used in fault diagnosis of the aircraft wing skin to prove feasibility of WPNN. The results show that the WPNN is feasible and has better performance in prediction accuracy.

Author Keywords: weighted probabilistic neural network, sensitivity analysis, compensating factors, weighted coefficients

articleTitle: State Recognition of Switch Matrix Based on Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: There are often many switches on the control panel of the equipment, especially the complex equipment such as the aircraft, spacecraft and so on. Catastrophic accident may happen even if one of the switches is set to the wrong state before the flight or during the flying process. It is necessary to develop some methods to monitor the states of the switches and give an alarm once the switch state is set mistakenly. Intuitively, a good design of mutual lock can partly solve this problem. However, some human errors cannot be detected only using this system. In this paper, we propose a switch matrix state recognition method based on image processing for an aircraft. The characteristics of the switch matrix are analyzed firstly. A standard to determine the state of the switch is proposed. Then, we propose a state detection process of the rocker switch. First of all, the working area of a switch is calculated by comparing the working area color with the background color after a series of image processing. Then, the switch head area can be segmented by means of color segmentation, denoising, median filtering and so on. By comparing the switch head area and the background, we can calculate the relative position between them, which means that the state of the switch can be determined. If the state of the switch matrix is not as expected, an alarm is given. The method is applied on an airplane control panel, which shows that it has the potential to be used to the switch matrix.

Author Keywords: rocker switch, image processing, switch state recognition, switch matrix

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Phased Mission System Based on Micro-Replacment Fault Tree
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: With the extensive application of phased mission system (PMS), the study of phased mission characteristics becomes more and more necessary and urgent. Considering the multi-mode failure of equipment, this paper proposes a reliability modeling and prediction method based on the micro-replacement fault tree, which is used to solve the reliability analysis problem of phased mission system. We take a typical phased mission system as an example to verify the feasibility of the method. This method provides a simpler and more efficient way to evaluate the reliability of complex systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Fault Monitoring Method Based on Acceleration Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: With the continuous progress of the space station project, the rotary mechanism is widely used in the space station. Serious failure of rotating mechanism can cause motor burnout and then safety problems. Therefore, it is necessary to monitor and diagnose rotating mechanism. The vibration signal of the rotating mechanism is nonlinear and non-stationary. Therefore, the acceleration sensor vibration signal is decomposed by CEEMD method to get the intrinsic mode function. Next, Fourier transform is used to obtain time-frequency information according to the obvious components of fault characteristics, and the information entropy of time-frequency information is calculated. The degree of dimensionality reduction about fault feature is determined by selecting the number of principal components through adaptive cumulative contribution. Finally, the fault feature is trained by support vector machine and tested with data. Experimental results show that the optimized method is less computational and can accurately extract fault feature information.

Author Keywords: CEEMD, fault feature, principal component analysis, support vector machines

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on Empirical Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Rotating machinery is one of the key components in mechanical equipment. Once the rotating machinery failed, it would lead to economic losses, or even a serious safety accident. Therefore, rotating machinery fault diagnosis has attracted a great deal of attention. Since the fault vibration signal of the rotating machinery is a mixture of different frequency components, signal decomposition methods have become powerful tools to extract the local information of the fault signal. Empirical wavelet transform (EWT) is an effective and self-adaptive signal decomposition method which has been widely studied. However, seldom of them attempt to conduct a systematic study on the performance of the EWT in terms of signal decomposition. In this paper, we perform the systematic simulations on how the retrieval performance of EWT is affected by the two-dimensional parameters, amplitude ratio and frequency ratio. By comparing the decomposition components with the original ones, we obtain the results which could guide people to evaluate the EWT method. Finally, the applicable region of the EWT in the fault diagnosis on rotating machinery are discussed.

articleTitle: Reliability Testing Method for Subway Trains Acceptance Based on Bayesian Theory Modified by Fibonacci Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The reliability testing method for subway trains acceptance based on Bayesian theory mainly uses prior information, the data of reliability testing for qualification acceptance, and the posterior information is obtained according to Bayesian estimation formula. Finally, the reliability testing method for subway trains acceptance is established. For the problem that some reliability testing method for subway trains acceptance cannot truly reflect the reliability level of subway trains, this paper uses the Fibonacci iteration algorithm to modify the parameters in reliability testing method for production acceptance based on Bayesian theory. The results demonstrate that the Fibonacci algorithm can truly reflect the actual train failure rate, and the reliability testing method for subway trains acceptance proposed in this paper can significantly shorten the test time.

articleTitle: Application of Adaptive Mono-Stable Stochastic Resonance Based on Cuckoo Search for Incipient Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Element Bearings
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Bearings are the main components of the modern machinery. Poor operating environment often makes them prone to failure, which may cause significant economic losses and catastrophic disasters. Once the incipient fault appears, the machinery will not operate correctly, and even go down. Therefore, detecting their incipient fault as soon as possible is useful for bearing prognostics and health management. According to stochastic resonance theory, the weak signal can be enhanced with the assistance of proper noise in a proper nonlinear system. Therefore, stochastic resonance is suited for fault diagnosis. In this paper, an adaptive mono-stable stochastic resonance based on cuckoo search is proposed for incipient bearing fault diagnosis. The exponential type single-well system is used as the nonlinear system of the mono-stable stochastic resonance. The bearing fault signal after pre-processing is processed by the mono-stable stochastic resonance. The cuckoo search is used to search the optimal parameters of the nonlinear system. The signal-to-noise ratio is used as the evaluation of stochastic resonance. Finally, we conducted two bearing fault test to validate the effectiveness of proposed methods. The results meet the expected effect of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Root Cause Identification Approach Based on FP-Growth for Product Quality Accident
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The Product Quality Accident (PQA) is a kind of accident mainly caused by product quality defects originated in design and production. To decrease the number and the severity of PQA in usage is a routine task of quality and reliability engineer. Especially with the advent of the era of intelligent manufacturing and big data, the functional structure of product is becoming increasingly complicated and the dimension of big data in product lifecycle is high. As a result, it is difficult to artificially identify the root cause of PQA by traditional method. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel method based on an advanced data mining algorithm for root cause identification. Firstly, the quality accident formation mechanism is introduced in detail. Secondly, with the aid of the domain mapping theory, PQA relevance tree is contributed. Thirdly, with the setting of reasonable support and confidence, the FP-Growth algorithm is used to further mine the relevance rules and construct a complete PQA relevance tree, which could reduce the ambiguity of PQA root cause identification. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed technique is verified by a root cause analysis example of an engine quality accident.

Author Keywords: Product quality accidents, Root cause analysis, Axiomatic design, FP-Growth algorithm

articleTitle: Simulation Research on Traffic Flow Characteristics of Bus Stop Area Based on VISSIM Software
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Under the background of implementing the "public transit priority" strategy, it is of great significance to study the traffic flow in the bus stop area to solve traffic problems. Based on the field research, this paper uses VISSIM simulation software to study the common influence of bus arrival frequency and nonmotor vehicle traffic volume on traffic flow in bus stop area under the premise of fixed motor vehicle traffic. Considering the actual situation that the amount of nonmotor vehicles grows rapidly, especially the sharing bicycles, the delay time of mixed traffic flow and service level of nonmotor vehicle lane are used as evaluation indicators. In this paper, three representative station types are selected for simulation research. They are the linear type stop placed next to the nonmotor vehicle lanes, the linear type stop that the nonmotor vehicle lane bypasses after the platform and the harbor type stop set next to the nonmotor vehicle lane. Finally, combined with the simulation results, a reasonable station type optimization plan is proposed for the Pengyuan Ximen Bus Station in Xuzhou to reduce the conflict of mixed traffic flow in the bus station area and improve the service level of the bus station.

Author Keywords: bus stop, type of stop, mixed traffic flow, VISSIM simulation

articleTitle: Optimal Similarity Measurement for Discriminant Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: similarity measurements are vital in classifier design used for pattern recognition tasks. Representative vector machines (RVMs), which assign the test example according to its nearest representative vector, can be viewed as a framework of typical classifiers such as the nearest neighbor (NN) classifiers, support vector machines (SVMs), sparse representation-based classification (SRC). This paper attempts to employ a variety of similarity measurements to observe the performance of discriminant vector machines (DVMs), which are motivated from RVMs. The experiments conducted on Yale and ORL databases show that L3 norm outperforms the traditional L2 norm. Furthermore, some other similarity measurements are summarized preliminarily. This work is not only a further study of DVMs, but also a worthy perspective to optimize other classifiers.

Author Keywords: similarity measurements, Representative Vector Machines (RVMs), Discriminant Vector Machines (DVMs)

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Slice Spectral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Higher-order spectral analysis can suppress Gaussian noise effectively, and Hilbert envelope analysis can demodulate the fault modulation frequency. In order to analyze the fault vibration signal of mechanical products accurately, in this paper the advantages of higher-order spectrum and Hilbert envelope analysis are combined. Firstly, the Hilbert envelope analysis of the vibration signal is performed to obtain the envelope of the signal. Then the envelope is analyzed by bispectrum. At last the nonlinear characteristics resulting from the secondary phase coupling can be extracted to obtain the fault characteristic frequency. Through a case study, the method proposed in this paper is verified, which makes effective diagnosis of the bearing failure.

Author Keywords: Bispectrum Hilbert Envelope Analysis, Fault Diagnosis, Bearing Failure

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Adaptive Multiclass–Mahalanobis–Taguchi System
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: To diagnose faults of bearings accurately, a fault diagnosis method based on Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and adaptive Multiclass-Mahalanobis-Taguchi System (aMMTS) is proposed in this paper. The condition of the bearing is monitored in real time by sensors. Then, the vibration signal is decomposed by EMD and the features are extracted by using SVD. Then, a novel adaptive Multiclass-Mahalanobis-Taguchi system is proposed for fault diagnosis. The hybrid method based on EMD-SVD and adaptive Multiclass-Mahalanobis-Taguchi system overcomes the shortcomings in the Mahalanobis-Taguchi system in terms of over-fitting and non-adaptive feature selection for fault diagnosis and has some advantages over the traditional auxiliary noise fault analysis method when dealing with nonlinear signal, and can diagnose the bearing fault without manual intervention. The effectivity and feasibility of the proposed method is validated by an experiment.

Author Keywords: fault diagnosis, bearing, SVD, EMD, adaptive Multiclass–Mahalanobis–Taguchi System

articleTitle: Analysis of Radiation Effects for Monitoring Circuit Based on Deep Belief Network and Support Vector Method
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The monitoring circuit is widely applied in radiation environment and it is of significance to study the circuit reliability with the radiation effects. In this paper, an intelligent analysis method based on Deep Belief Network (DBN) and Support Vector Method is proposed according to the radiation experiments analysis of the monitoring circuit. The Total Ionizing Dose (TID) of the monitoring circuit is used to identify the circuit degradation trend. Firstly, the output waveforms of the monitoring circuit are obtained by radiating with the different TID. Subsequently, the Deep Belief Network Model is trained to extract the features of the circuit signal. Finally, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Support Vector Regression (SVR) are applied to classify and predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of the monitoring circuit. According to the experimental results, the performance of DBN-SVM exceeds DBN method for feature extraction and classification, and SVR is effective for predicting the degradation.

Author Keywords: monitoring circuit, Deep Belief Network, Support Vector Machine, Support Vector Regression, radiation effects

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Extreme Learning Machine, Least Squares Support Vector Machine, Back Propagation Neural Network for Outlet Total Phosphorus Prediction
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Phosphorus is the main factor causing the degradation and eutrophication, which is important to strictly limit the emission of total phosphorus (TP) in wastewater treatment. Prediction outlet quality is an effective way to improve the monitoring level of sewage treatment. However, it is difficult to establish the mathematical model to predict outlet TP accurately because of the complex and changeable environment and the interrelated operation variables of sewage treatment. In this paper, three different data driven methods, extreme learning machine (ELM), least squares support vector machine (LS-SVM) regression method, and back propagation neural network (BPNN) are used for prediction of outlet TP concentration (TP(out)) base on observed data of inlet factors in sewage treatment plant, respectively. To get more accurate evaluation results of the ELM, LS-SVM and BPNN models, three quantitative standard statistical performance evaluation measures, mean square error (MSE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), are employed. The results show that the ELM method has remarkably superior performance on TP(<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">out</sub>) prediction than peer models in outlet prediction of wastewater treatment.

Author Keywords: extreme learning machine, least squares support vector machine, back propagation neural network, total phosphorus, prediction

articleTitle: An Indirect On-line Measurement Method of Crankshaft Clearance Based on Simulation Vibration Signal
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Monitoring the clearance size between the connecting rod big end bearing shell and the crankshaft, and grasping the health status of the equipment operation are of great significance to realize the prediction and maintenance of reciprocating compressor. If the clearance is too small, the friction will be too large and even stuck when the bearing shell and the crankshaft are moving relatively. Conversely, if the clearance is too big, it will not only affect the motion accuracy of the mechanism but also aggravate bearing shell wear, and even cause serious faults or accidents. However, the crankshaft clearance is difficult to be measured directly during the compressor running due to the influence of complex mechanical structure. Aim at this problem, an indirect on-line measurement method of crankshaft clearance based on simulation vibration signal is proposed in this paper. In this method, the dynamic simulation of the running process of the reciprocating compressor motion pair in ideal state is realized by using the virtual prototyping technology. The simulation results show that the shock of the crosshead decreases first and then increases with the increase of the clearance size, and there is a clearance range that makes the equipment run relatively smoothly. According to the simulation results, the mapping relation model of crankshaft clearance size and simulation vibration signal is set up, and the indirect measurement of the crankshaft clearance is realized by the comparison of the actual acquisition vibration signal and the model. This method provides a new idea and method for the diagnosis of reciprocating compressor crankshaft clearance fault.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis and RUL Prediction Strategy Based on Double Time-Scale Particle Filter for Nonlinear Electromechanical System
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: In order to achieve fault diagnosis and remaining useful life prediction effectively when system states and fault parameters run at two different time-scales, a double time-scale particle filter algorithm is proposed to jointly estimate the system states and the possible fault parameters. The bond graph model that deals with various energy forms in a unified way is constructed to carry out fault diagnosis which consists of fault detection and isolation through deducing analytical redundancy relations to calculate residual of system. The fault estimation is used to identify the parameters of the isolated fault set and determine the true fault as well as remaining useful life prediction. Since the fault parameters exhibit slow-time varying characteristics and the system states show quick-time varying characteristics, the double time-scale particle filter is developed to simultaneously estimate and predict the system states and parameters on two different time scales for diagnosis and prognosis purpose. The effectiveness of the proposed double time-scale particle filter algorithm is validated by the simulation results on the nonlinear electromechanical system.

articleTitle: Detection of Planetary Carrier Cracks Using the Time Domain Synchronous Averaging
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: This paper aims to detect planetary carrier cracks through the vibration sensors mounted on the stationary gearbox housing. The spacing of the planet gears related to the rotating carrier plate is unequal, because of the crack on the planetary carrier. In this paper, the time domain synchronous averaging method is utilized to detect the fault. This method tends to eliminate any machining error and frequency components not concerned with carrier crack. And then, observation of spectrum sidebands is employed to extract cracked planetary carrier fault features. Finally, through comparing different rotational speed of planetary carrier, the effect of rotational speed of planetary carrier on detecting is researched. Tests are carried out to verify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault Diagnosis Observer-Based Fault Tolerant Control Design for a Jumbo Jet Transport Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: An adaptive fault diagnosis observer-based fault tolerant control method is proposed for the actuator faults of a jumbo jet transport aircraft. This method not only can simplify design procedures, but also can guarantee good performance when part of the actuators fails. Considering the linear motion characteristics of flight mode for the jumbo jet transport aircraft, a linear model is firstly established in state space using the small perturbation method. Then, a novel augmented fault diagnosis observer design is introduced to relax the strictly positive real (SPR) requirement of the system. Meanwhile, considering their performances simultaneously, a dynamical output feedback fault tolerant control design, which can be designed separately from the fault diagnosis observer, is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through its application to the simulated longitudinal motion of the Boeing 747-100/200.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling of the Aircraft Landing Gear Based on ISD Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic modeling for an aircraft landing gear based on the Inerter-Spring-Damper (ISD) mechanism (including inerter, spring and damper). The inerter is a mechanical element proposed recently, which has two terminals movable freely and independently. The force across these two terminals is proportional to the relative acceleration. Performance could be improved by introducing ISD mechanism into various suspension systems, which has been observed. In theory, introducing the inerter into the aircraft landing gear can improve the performance of touchdown and taxiing effectively, and reduce the failure probability. This paper discusses the fundamental principles of the inerter, and the ISD structures in details. The study makes use of computer simulations and establishes the dynamic model of the landing gear based on ISD mechanism, and the dynamic characteristics during taxiing is analyzed.

articleTitle: Study on the Integration Experiment and Evaluation Methods of Ship Electrical Equipment Testability
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of large samples, fault injection difficulties, high risks, long period and low conclusion credibility in the testability evaluation of ship electrical equipment, this paper presents an integrated experiment technology based on the synthesis of virtual simulation, semi-physical testing and physical prototype testing. This article builds an integrated testability evaluation model based on multi-source data fusion. Finally, the feasibility and rationality of proposed method are verified by taking typical ship electrical equipment as example. This method would provide technical support for the efficient evaluation of the testability level of the ship electrical equipment.

Author Keywords: electrical equipment, testability, integration experiment and evaluation

articleTitle: A Simulation Based Band-Pass Filter to Improve the Polynomial Chirplet Transform in Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Bearings are the basic components in mechanical or hydraulic power transmission systems. Defects in bearings will lead to a sudden stoppage of machines. In this paper, we develop a new fault detection method based on the numerical simulation determined band-pass filter and polynomial chirplet transform (PCT). Using band-pass filter, the sub-signal containing the information of fault feature is preserved and further decomposed by PCT to obtain time-frequency spectrum with higher signal to noise ratio (SNR). To design the efficient band-pass filter, the input center frequency is predetermined by finite element simulations. To improve the performance of the traditional chirplet transform (CT), a polynomial kernel function is employed to construct one of the parameterized time-frequency analysis methods, i.e., PCT. PCT reconstructs the time-frequency spectrum along the frequency trajectory so that the energy distribution on the spectrum is concentrated around the real instantaneous frequency of the signal. Thus, the PCT generates high time-frequency resolution, which is suitable for weak fault detection. The effectiveness of the proposed method in fault diagnosis is demonstrated by applications for vibration signal collected from bearings in both mechanical and hydraulic power transmission systems.

articleTitle: Study on Partial Stratified Resampling for Particle Filter Based Prognosis on Li-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Accurate online prognosis of engineering systems plays a vital role in prognosis and health management (PHM) technologies to ensure safety, prevent damage and economic loss. The particle filter (PF) algorithm has proved to be an effective method for prognostics. However, the PF algorithm suffers from serious particle degeneracy and particle impoverishment problems. Most of the studies in the literature focus on solving the particle degeneracy problem but at a heavy computational cost. In this study, we aim to explore the time efficient Partial Stratified Resampling algorithm which can be used for online state estimation problems and compare it with conventional Stratified Resampling algorithms. The accuracy and precision of the algorithms are validated using the lithium-ion battery data sets from CALCE® research group.

articleTitle: Adaptive Canonical Variate Analysis for Machine Fault Detection and Identification
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Canonical variable analysis (CVA) has been extensively applied to monitor industrial processes. However, conventional CVA is unable to handle the characteristics of time-varying processes. To address the limitations of the standard CVA for systems with time-varying properties, adaptive canonical variate analysis (ACVA) together with the first order perturbation theory are employed in this paper to detect faults in rotating machines. A bias-corrected exponentially weighted moving average approach is used in combination with the ACVA-based contributions to identify variables that are closely related to faults. The performance of the proposed technique is illustrated with condition monitoring data acquired from an operational centrifugal compressor. The results indicate that the proposed method can effectively detect and diagnose faults in real industrial systems under time-varying operating conditions.

Author Keywords: adaptive canonical variate analysis, fault detection, fault identification, process monitoring

articleTitle: Research on Missile Weapons Health Management and Storage Life Prediction Methods Based on PHM Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The application of PHM technology in missile weapons storage life prediction is one of the focuses of domestic and international research in recent years. Based on the analysis of the application methods of PHM, the overall framework of the reliability assessment and life prediction of missiles was established, the design ideas of data acquisition system and database system were given, the storage life prediction method of missile weapon based on data driven, physical model and prediction model was proposed. The result of research provides technical supports for the life extension and maintenance of missile weapons.

articleTitle: Research on Armored Equipment Autonomic Logistics Mode Based on PHM Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: By learning from the concept of autonomic logistics for aviation equipment and aiming at the characteristics of armored equipment, an autonomic logistics mode for armored equipment based on prognostic and health management (PHM) technology was proposed, and the architecture and working principle of armored equipment autonomic logistics mode were briefly described. The preliminary design of the two key technologies (PHM technology and Joint Distributed Information System) that support the autonomic logistics mode was carried out, providing preliminary technical support for the realization of the autonomic logistics of armored equipment.

Author Keywords: autonomic logistics, armored equipment, PHM (Prognostic and Health Management), JDIS (Joint Distributed Information System)

articleTitle: A Classification of Milling TCM Based on Bandpass Filter and Kernel Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Tool condition monitoring (TCM) plays an important role in milling process. An accurate TCM system not only improves the quality of products, but also helps improving the processing efficiency. Distinguishing the condition of tool wear effectively is a central part in the TCM. In this paper, a tool condition classification based on Bandpass Filter and Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (KELM) is proposed. Firstly, the Bandpass Filter is used to enhance the noise-signal ratio of original signals which are detected by cutting force and acoustic emission sensors. Then several statistical features of time and frequency domain for the preprocessed data are calculated. Finally, the KELM classifier is applied to identify the tool wear state. Experiment shows that the proposed method has outperformed the KELM-based method with different type's signals.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Fault Diagnosis Method for Rolling Element Bearings Based on Dynamic Model and Fast Spectral Kurtosis
publicationTitle: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: Quantitative analysis of rolling bearing fault is a crucial issue in the condition monitoring of rotating machines.
